title: SeqLen-aware kernel choreographer for mixed-precision attention tiling
creator: Jared Patel
description: Background: Our current kernel selection uses static heuristics that target average latency across mixed workloads. As customers run mixed-precision models and widely varying sequence lengths, we observe suboptimal kernel choices for medium-length prefill (128-1024 tokens) and bursty decode traffic, increasing p50 latency and token cost. Goal: Implement a lightweight 'choreographer' that picks attention kernel tiling and precision mode (fp16/int8 where supported) per-request by combining arch capabilities, sequence-length bucketing, and a compact online tuner. Success metrics: reduce p50 latency by >=10% for 128-1024 prefills on A100/GR8, reduce per-token GPU cost by >=6% across mixed workloads, keep tail (p95) regressions <=2% relative to baseline. Scope: runtime-only changes (kernel selection + small telemetry), opt-in via runtime flag, backwards-compatible defaults. Not in scope: model graph rewrites, new kernel implementations. Approach: 1) Bucket incoming requests by prefill length and token-phase profile (prefill vs decode mix). 2) For each bucket maintain a compact profile with recent latency/cost samples and a small exploration budget. 3) Candidate set includes tiling params (MxN tiling for attention), kernel impl (vendor-optimized vs fallback), and precision mode where hardware supports quantized kernels. 4) Use an episodic bandit (epsilon-greedy with conservative guardrails) to quickly prefer low-latency combos while retaining ability to explore after workload drift. 5) Safety: enforce SLO constraints via a runtime threshold, auto-roll back candidate choices that exceed latency or error budgets. Implementation plan: - Phase 0: telemetry collection and bucket definitions (2 weeks) - Phase 1: local simulator + microbench harness to validate choices across seqlen combos (1 week) - Phase 2: in-runtime choreographer with in-memory profiles and simple exploration (2 weeks) - Phase 3: gradual rollout (canary -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) with opt-out control plane flags (1 week) Key trade-offs: - Simpler tuners converge faster but may miss niche combos; full Bayesian approaches would be more optimal but heavier. - Per-request decision cost must be amortized; we prioritize a very cheap lookup + occasional probe. Observability: add per-bucket KPI (p50, p95, tokens/sec, kernel-choice-rate), sample traces linking request->kernel. Rollout plan: gated behind runtime-1.19 feature flag; initial canary on dedicated clusters for internal traffic then expand. Documentation: design doc in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/SeqLen+Choreographer and design notes in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/u/0/folders/1SeqlenChoreography
comments: 2026-03-02 - Jared Patel: Initial analysis shows a 14% p50 regression in A100 prefill 256-512 when using fallback generic tiling. Collected microbench traces from infra-runner cluster. Attached sampling script to Drive.

2026-03-04 - Leo Wang: Prototype simulator completed. Microbench results: for 256 token prefill on A100, MxN tile (32x128) + fp16 kernel gives 12% p50 improvement vs baseline; int8 path gives additional 3% but increases error in some opt kernels. Filed risk note and will gate int8 behind quantization-compat flag.
2026-03-05 - Marina Ortega (PM): Prioritize prefill buckets 128-1024, customer-impact scoreboard updated. Recommend canary on runtime-dedicated infra used by internal dashboards first.

2026-03-07 - Eng Review: Decided to use epsilon-greedy with epsilon=0.05 for exploration; incorporate decay and a minimum sample count of 50 before promoting a candidate. Action: add telemetry counters for sample count per candidate.

2026-03-09 - Leo Wang: Implemented safe rollback: if p95 for a bucket increases by >2x baseline for 10-minute window, revert to previous kernel and mark candidate as blacklisted for 1h. Added PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321

2026-03-10 - QA: Ran cluster-level soak for 6 hours under synthetic mixed load. Observed overall p50 improvement 9.8% and token cost reduction 5.3% - close to targets. Noted small p95 bump (1.1%) in a decode-heavy synthetic trace; investigating decode scheduling interaction. Next: tweak decode probe cadence and add metric alerting before canary.

Open questions: whether to bake hardware topology awareness (NUMA/chiplet) into bucket keys; start without it and treat as follow-on if we hit mismatch cases. Also decide long-term whether to replace epsilon-greedy with a Thompson sampling bandit when we have more telemetry.
